source.title: Learning curves theory of hierarchically compositional data with power-law distributed features

record.tranche_reason: Tests learning-curve scaling in a new setting: synthetic hierarchically compositional datasets generated by a random hierarchy model, using CNNs for classification and transformers for next-token prediction.
record.gate_note: The study reports empirical learning curves on synthetic data. Classification results measure test error, not cross-entropy loss; they bear on V7's curve-shape and setup dependence, but not V1. The next-token prediction experiments report test cross-entropy against training-set size. The study does not sweep parameter count or compute, test compute-optimal allocation, or test downstream-task performance. The sℓ-gram loss calculations in Figure 5 are not rows because they are not trained-model learning curves.
record.test_reason: The study trains CNNs and transformers on synthetic hierarchical (RHM/PCFG) data and measures test error or cross-entropy against training-set size. Its own results bear on V1 (data-axis power law of next-token loss) and on V7 (whether the exponent and curve shape depend on data structure). It is a new setting, not a replication of the original method.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that for classification the uniform-rule learning curve is sigmoidal, and Zipf-distributed rules turn it into a power law P^(-a/(1+a)) after a hierarchy-controlled pre-asymptotic phase. For next-token prediction the exponent is set by the hierarchy (Eq. 12), and the Zipf exponent changes only local details and the limiting loss L∞. The authors propose hierarchical structure as the explanation for LLM scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains CNNs and transformers on synthetic probabilistic-context-free-grammar data and varies training-set size and production-rule distributions. It does not reproduce the original studies' language-model sweeps over parameters, tokens, and compute or their compute-optimal allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with task (classification versus next-token prediction), Zipf exponent, hierarchy layer carrying the Zipf distribution, hierarchy depth, branching factor, and number of production rules.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: Experiments use simplified synthetic hierarchical data rather than natural datasets; parameter-count and compute sweeps are absent. Curves are presented in figures without stated error bars in the reported results. CNN results average over 10 instances for m≤20 and 3 for m>20; transformer results average over 8 instances, but uncertainty intervals are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional trained-model learning-curve results were omitted. Figure 5's sℓ-gram cross-entropies are calculated grammar-level quantities rather than trained-model curves, so they are described in gate_note rather than entered as rows.

untested.parts: Parameter-count and compute axes; natural-language pretraining; real-scale LMs. Only the training-set-size axis is tested, on synthetic RHM data over roughly 2-4 decades of P.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. The appendix only notes that more channels or heads do not change results in the data-limited regime.
No image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer experiments.
No parameter counting, schedule or fitting-method comparison, and no comparison of published laws. Only data-structure dependence is tested.

record.verdict_notes: Mainly a theory paper with empirical confirmation drawn in figures. No fitted exponents or error bars are reported; agreement is with predicted or guide lines. The CNN classification rows measure test error on a classifier, not LM pretraining loss, so their bearing on V7 is indirect. The model-size results (H>512 and nh up to 64 change nothing) only establish the data-limited regime. Figure 5 sℓ-gram losses are computed, not trained, and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Only test cross-entropy versus training-set size is tested, on synthetic RHM data. Parameter-count and compute scaling, natural-language pretraining, and whether other resource axes are non-bottlenecks are not tested. In the one-layer experiment, the reported power law is for loss above the s-gram entropy.
The study uses synthetic hierarchical sequences, but does not test other modalities or training regimes such as image/video training, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No parameter-count or compute-optimal allocation exponents, fitting-method comparison, or comparison of published laws is tested.

relationships.condition: Synthetic RHM next-token prediction with small transformers; training-set-size axis, data-limited regime
relationships.reason: Test cross-entropy decays as a power law in P. In the depth-1 case (r23, r24) this holds for excess loss over L1(a). In the depth-4 case (r25-r28) it matches the Eq. 12 asymptote.
relationships.display_finding: Test cross-entropy decayed as a power law in training-set size, applying to excess loss above L1(a) at depth 1 and matching the theoretical asymptote at depth 4.

source_check.reason: Figures 4 and 6 support power-law decay toward a residual loss in this synthetic language setting; the plotted scaling concerns excess loss.

relationships.condition: RHM root classification (CNNs, test error) and depth-1 next-token prediction
relationships.reason: The exponent a/(1+a) tracks the data's Zipf exponent (r2-r4, r12-r14, r23, r24). Uniform rules give sigmoidal, non-power-law curves (r1, r11). A hierarchy-set pre-asymptotic phase scales with vm^(L-1) (r7-r10, r18-r21).
relationships.display_finding: The exponent a/(1+a) tracks the data's Zipf exponent, uniform rules produce sigmoidal curves, and the hierarchy determines a pre-asymptotic phase scaling as vm^(L−1).

relationships.condition: Deep-transformer next-token prediction; Zipf-layer placement in classification
relationships.reason: In deep next-token prediction the exponent is invariant to the rule distribution and is set by the hierarchy; only the limiting loss shifts (r26-r28). Zipf-layer placement leaves classification curves similar (r5, r6, r15-r17).
relationships.display_finding: Deep next-token prediction retained a hierarchy-determined exponent across rule distributions while its limiting loss shifted; changing Zipf-layer placement also left classification curves similar.
